userStories.title: Flow steps and review tasks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Define the fixed step vocabulary and exact tasks used by the two flow review agents.

**Motivation** — F3 builds that engine for one feature; verdict classification and spec fixes (F4), multi-feature order and merge waits (F5) and the web pages (F6) build on it.

**Approach** — Pure module `flow-steps.ts`: `FlowStep`, `FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION`, `FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX` and `buildReviewTask(step, specPath, feature)`.

Review agent = api setting. `FLEET_FLOW_REVIEW_AGENT` (default `Explore`) names the nax agent of both review steps; the model is always the flow's `reviewerRole`; the task starts with `/spec-review` so nax expands the skill.

The verdict instruction appended to both review tasks:
```text
When you are done, end your reply with exactly one JSON object on its own line, with no text after it:
{"findings":[{"id":"<short id>","summary":"<one sentence>"}]}
Use {"findings":[]} when you found nothing that should change before the next step.
```
Keep the quoted verdict instruction, including its empty-findings example; ensure the exact line `{"findings":[]}` is also present, without surrounding spaces, to satisfy the instruction AC. Do not add invented runtime rejection behavior for inputs outside the existing validated path/feature contract. Build SPEC_REVIEW as `/spec-review <specPath>` and PRD_REVIEW as `/spec-review --spec <specPath> --prd .nax/features/<feature>/prd.json`, followed by a blank line and the exported instruction. Respect the existing 16,384-character AGENT task bound.

**Scope** — In: the pure step constants and review-task builder, with colocated unit tests. Out: parsing verdicts (US-002), dispatch-body construction (US-010), and config resolution (US-017).

**Interface** — `FlowStep` (`'SPEC_REVIEW' | 'PLAN' | 'PRD_REVIEW' | 'RUN' | 'REVIEW' | 'FIX'`), `FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION`, `FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX` (2000), `buildReviewTask(step, specPath, feature)`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] buildReviewTask('SPEC_REVIEW', '.nax/features/a/spec.md', 'a') returns `/spec-review .nax/features/a/spec.md`, a blank line, then FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION.
[unit] buildReviewTask('PRD_REVIEW', '.nax/features/a/spec.md', 'a') returns `/spec-review --spec .nax/features/a/spec.md --prd .nax/features/a/prd.json`, a blank line, then FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION.
[unit] buildReviewTask('SPEC_REVIEW', p, 'a') for a 400-character spec path p returns at most 16,384 characters.
[unit] FLOW_VERDICT_INSTRUCTION includes the line `{"findings":[]}`.
[unit] FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX equals 2000.
[unit] buildReviewTask('SPEC_REVIEW', '.nax/features/a/spec.md', 'a') does not include the PRD-only --spec or --prd flags.

routing.reasoning: Pure additive constants and deterministic string construction, using existing agent bounds.

userStories.title: The verdict parser
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse a review agent's final JSON verdict and produce bounded stop details for findings.

**Motivation** — F3 builds that engine for one feature; verdict classification and spec fixes (F4), multi-feature order and merge waits (F5) and the web pages (F6) build on it.

**Approach** — Review steps stop strictly. F3 reads only the final verdict JSON of a review `AGENT` job. No findings: the flow continues. Any finding, or no parseable verdict: the flow stops with the findings in its detail. F4 replaces "any finding stops" with classify, fix and ask.

Verdict strictness. The verdict is the text from the last `{"findings"` to the end, after removing a trailing code fence and whitespace; any other trailing text makes it unreadable, as the instruction asks for nothing after it.

Stop details are at most 2,000 characters (`FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX`).

Require a findings array whose entries have string summary; keep id only when it is a string. Return `{ ok: false }` for null, absent JSON, malformed JSON, a non-array findings property or an entry without summary. Format one finding as `1 finding: 1. a`, multiple findings as `2 findings: 1. [F1] a 2. b`, and truncate overlong output to exactly 2,000 characters ending in `…`.

**Scope** — In: pure parser/formatter and unit tests. Out: decision transitions (US-008), AGENT dispatch (US-010). Verdict classification (`answered`/`minor`/`ambiguous`), spec-fix jobs, batched questions, agent rulings on open PR items and the flow's ticket (fleet flow F4).

**Interface** — `FlowFinding`, `parseFlowVerdict(output)` and `formatFindings(findings)` in `flow-verdict.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parseFlowVerdict('Looks good.\n{"findings":[]}') returns { ok: true, findings: [] }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict of text ending in `{"findings":[{"id":"F1","summary":"Missing AC for 409"}]}` returns ok true with the one finding { id: 'F1', summary: 'Missing AC for 409' }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":[{"summary":"x"}]}\nmore text\n{"findings":[]}') returns ok true with no findings.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":[]}\n```\n  ') returns ok true with no findings.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":[]} thanks') returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('All fine, no JSON.') returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict(null) returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings": oops') returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":{"a":1}}') returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":[{"id":"F1"}]}') returns { ok: false }.
[unit] parseFlowVerdict('{"findings":[{"id":7,"summary":"s"}]}') returns ok true with the one finding { summary: 's' }.
[unit] formatFindings([{ id: 'F1', summary: 'a' }, { summary: 'b' }]) returns `2 findings: 1. [F1] a 2. b`.
[unit] formatFindings([{ summary: 'a' }]) returns `1 finding: 1. a`.
[unit] formatFindings of 100 findings of 100 characters each returns exactly 2,000 characters ending in `…`.

routing.reasoning: Bounded untrusted-output parsing and formatting with fully specified deterministic cases; no auth or credential handling.

userStories.title: Flow job columns and flow stop/re-ask
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist flow-job linkage and stop detail, and make stop/re-ask update all feature states.

**Motivation** — F1 (`fleet-flow-record`, #400) records flows and their one approval, and F2 (`fleet-agent-job`, #403) added the `AGENT` job kind, but nothing moves an approved flow: `FleetFlowStartCommand.execute` and the thread tick both leave it `APPROVED` and stop.

**Approach** — One migration adds `FleetJob.flowId` (nullable, relation to `FleetFlow` with `onDelete: SetNull`, index on `flowId, queuedAt`), `FleetJob.flowStep` (nullable string), `FleetFlow.stopDetail` (nullable string) and the index `FleetFlow(state, id)`. `FleetFlowRecord` gains optional `stopDetail`. `PrismaFleetFlowRepository.stop` takes an optional `detail` and stops every feature; `reask` resets every feature to `PENDING` with no `currentStep`.

A human stop does not cancel the running job (design, Stops). The record phase writes nothing when the flow has meanwhile left `APPROVED`/`RUNNING`. `IFleetFlowRepository.stop` now also marks every feature `STOPPED`, for every caller.

Update the Prisma relation inverse and domain mapping; deploy this additive migration before selecting new columns. Use the preceding-schema scratch migration pattern for the migration test and existing flow repository/read-stop integration fixtures for behavior.

**Scope** — In: schema, migration, domain optional field and repository stop/reask semantics, retaining existing transition errors. Out: job dispatch/adoption (US-004), step repository (US-005/006). Every web page and the `FleetFlowDto` fields for steps, jobs and `stopDetail` (fleet flow F6), including the "cap excludes N jobs with unknown cost" display. Cancelling a running job when a flow stops or returns to `PENDING`: by design the flow only starts nothing more.

**Interface** — `stopDetail?: string | null`; `stop(id: string, reason: string, now: Date, detail?: string | null)` writes `stopDetail` (null when omitted) and sets every feature's `state` to `STOPPED`; `reask` also sets every feature's `state` to `PENDING` and `currentStep` to null.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] After the migration, a FleetJob inserted with flowId set to an existing flow's id and flowStep 'PLAN' reads back with both values.
[integration] Deleting a FleetFlow sets flowId to null on its jobs.
[integration] Deleting a FleetFlow deletes no job.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.stop(id, 'cost_cap', now, 'spent 5 of cap 5') returns a record with state STOPPED, stopReason cost_cap and stopDetail `spent 5 of cap 5`.
[integration] After stop(id, 'cost_cap', now, 'x'), every feature of that flow has state STOPPED.
[integration] stop(id, 'human_stop', now) without a detail stores stopDetail null.
[integration] stop on a PENDING flow, as FleetFlowsService.stop calls it, also sets its features to STOPPED.
[integration] reask(id, { specSha, approvalRequestId }) on a RUNNING flow whose feature is RUNNING at currentStep SPEC_REVIEW leaves the feature with state PENDING and currentStep null.
[integration] findById returns stopDetail from the row.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.stop(id, 'human_stop', now) on a COMPLETED flow rejects with FlowTransitionError, preserving the existing terminal-state transition restriction.

routing.reasoning: Five-file additive migration/domain/repository change follows existing transition and nested-write patterns; scratch-schema and repository DB tests cover SetNull and feature resets without a new orchestration abstraction.

userStories.title: Flow fields on jobs and the system key
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Link every dispatched or adopted flow job durably and register the flow engine's system audit key.

**Motivation** — F1 (`fleet-flow-record`, #400) records flows and their one approval, and F2 (`fleet-agent-job`, #403) added the `AGENT` job kind, but nothing moves an approved flow: `FleetFlowStartCommand.execute` and the thread tick both leave it `APPROVED` and stop.

**Approach** — The job row is the source of truth. Every flow job stores `flowId` and `flowStep` in the same insert that creates it. The engine reads the flow's latest job (by `queuedAt`) on every tick, so a crash between dispatch and the bookkeeping that follows loses nothing: the next tick sees the job. `FleetFlowFeature.state`, `currentStep` and `prNumber` are written after each dispatch; the `FIX` step reads `prNumber` from the feature.

`opts` adds `flowId?: string` and `flowStep?: FlowStep`, the `auditKey` union adds `'system.flow.advance'`, and both flow fields are written in the job insert. A new method `adoptForFlow(jobId: string, flowId: string, step: FlowStep): Promise<boolean>` sets them on an existing job whose `flowId` is null, through a new `IFleetJobRepository.adoptForFlow(jobId, flowId, step): Promise<boolean>` (a conditional update; `FleetJobPatch` does not carry `flowId`).

`NewFleetJob` and `FleetJobRecord`: both add optional `flowId?: string | null` and `flowStep?: string | null`. `buildAssignPayload` also gives a `PLAN` with a non-null `flowId` `expectBranch: job.ref`. Append `system.flow.advance` (`'any'`) right after `system.flow.respec` in NEW_KEY_SCOPES and add it to PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS until US-017 declares the ticker. Update catalog.spec.ts's mirrored table; every role in __snapshots__/role-matrix.json gains `"system.flow.advance": ["non-role-key","non-role-key"]` right after system.flow.respec, with no other entry changes; permission-contract.spec.ts expectedPending gains the key. Preserve all existing dispatch callers and current FK not-found mapping. Extend existing job integration/assign-payload unit suites.

**Scope** — In: dispatch opts/insert, domain mapping, conditional adoption, PLAN assignment including existing thread PLAN behavior, and permission-catalog contracts. Out: calling adoption in a record transaction (US-016), ticker declaration/removing the pending key (US-017), and public DTO changes. Mapping a `flowId` foreign-key failure at dispatch (a flow deleted mid-pass) to anything but the existing `createJob` not-found path. Regenerating the CLI client and CLI commands for flows; `openapi.json` does not change.

**Interface** — `adoptForFlow(jobId: string, flowId: string, step: FlowStep): Promise<boolean>` on FleetJobsService and IFleetJobRepository; dispatch opts add `flowId?: string`, `flowStep?: FlowStep` and audit key `'system.flow.advance'`.

[integration] FleetJobsService.dispatch without flowId creates a job whose flowId and flowStep are null.
[integration] A job created with flowId and read back through the job repository's findById carries flowId and flowStep.
[integration] FleetJobsService.adoptForFlow(jobId, flowId, 'REVIEW') on a job with no flowId sets both fields and returns true.
[integration] adoptForFlow on a job whose flowId is another flow's id writes nothing and returns false.
[unit] buildAssignPayload for a PLAN job with flowId flow-1, no threadId and ref feat/x sets expectBranch feat/x.
[unit] buildAssignPayload for a RUN job with flowId flow-1 sets no expectBranch.
[unit] buildAssignPayload for a PLAN job with neither threadId nor flowId sets no expectBranch.
[unit] findCatalogEntry('system.flow.advance') returns an entry with access system.
[unit] buildAssignPayload for a PLAN job with an existing threadId, no flowId and ref feat/x still sets expectBranch feat/x.

userStories.title: Step repository reads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide the durable reads needed to select live single-feature flows and reconstruct job progress and spend.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — `IFleetFlowStepRepository` (token `FLEET_FLOW_STEP_REPOSITORY`) and its Prisma implementation, read half: `listAdvanceable(limit, afterId)`, `latestJob(flowId)`, `latestJobForStep(flowId, step)`, `sumCost(flowId)` and `ingestSettled(jobId, leaseEpoch)`.

Cross-table reads in the flow's repository. The step repository reads `FleetJob`, `FleetBundleIngest`, `User` and `Agent` rows, as `PrismaScheduleRepository` already does for its cost totals and `findOwnerAccess`. The one write to `FleetJob` (adoption) goes through `FleetJobsService`.

Paging. `listAdvanceable(limit, afterId)` returns single-feature `APPROVED`/`RUNNING` flows ordered by `id`, after the given id; the ticker pages 50 at a time until a short page, at most 10 pages per tick. A new index `FleetFlow(state, id)` serves it.

Cap. `spentUsd` is recomputed on every tick as the sum of `costSpentUsd + costCarriedUsd` over jobs with the flow's id. Before any dispatch, a remaining cap (`costCapUsd - spentUsd`, rounded down to 4 decimals) below `0.0001` stops the flow (`cost_cap`); otherwise the remaining cap is the job's `maxCostUsd`. A job with unknown cost adds 0.

Latest jobs are selected by queuedAt, with latestJobForStep filtering the requested flowStep before ordering. Ingest settlement is tied to the exact job lease; done, partial and failed settle it. Use generated Prisma.Decimal for the sum and return four-place strings. Write DB-backed repository tests in the declared new suite; US-006 extends it.

**Scope** — In: repository token/interface, AdvanceableFlow, read implementation and integration cases. Out: creatorAccess and mutations (US-006), pure cap subtraction (US-010), ticker paging loop (US-017).

**Interface** — `FLEET_FLOW_STEP_REPOSITORY`, `IFleetFlowStepRepository`, `AdvanceableFlow`; `listAdvanceable(limit, afterId)`, `latestJob(flowId)`, `latestJobForStep(flowId, step)`, `sumCost(flowId)`, `ingestSettled(jobId, leaseEpoch)`.

[integration] listAdvanceable(50, null) omits a two-feature APPROVED flow.

userStories.title: Step repository writes and lookups
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add transaction-aware progress/spend/completion writes and creator existence/disabled lookups to the step repository.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — The step repository's other half: `setSpent(flowId, spentUsd)`, `creatorAccess(ref)`, `markStep(flowId, featureId, step, data)` and `complete(flowId, now)`.

Cross-table reads in the flow's repository. The step repository reads `FleetJob`, `FleetBundleIngest`, `User` and `Agent` rows, as `PrismaScheduleRepository` already does for its cost totals and `findOwnerAccess`. The one write to `FleetJob` (adoption) goes through `FleetJobsService`.

Read User.disabled for users, return exists false/disabled false for absent users, and determine agent existence without treating agent liveness as disabled. markStep writes the flow state and sets the specified feature RUNNING/currentStep; set prNumber only when supplied, preserving an existing value otherwise. complete writes COMPLETED and endedAt on the flow and COMPLETED on its feature. All methods use the transaction-scoped Prisma client so the advance service can audit mutations atomically. Extend the repository interface and the integration suite created by US-005.

**Scope** — In: creatorAccess, setSpent, markStep and complete. Out: evaluating effective permission keys/cap (US-014), the bookkeeping reason and audit orchestration (US-012), job adoption (US-004/016). Notifications on a flow stop or completion: until F4, a stop is visible only in flow activity, audit, `stopReason` and `stopDetail`.

**Interface** — `setSpent(flowId, spentUsd)`, `creatorAccess(ref)`, `markStep(flowId, featureId, step, data)` and `complete(flowId, now)` on IFleetFlowStepRepository.

userStories.title: Step decision, gating and job ends
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Establish the pure flow decision model, approval-epoch gate, active-job waiting and generic job-failure stops.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — Pure `decideFlowStep(input: FlowStepInput): FlowStepAction`, first part: the single-feature gate, the `APPROVED` start and adoption rule, waiting on an active job, and the stop rules for failed, cancelled, crashed and escalated jobs.

Multi-feature flows wait. F3 advances only flows with exactly one feature. A flow with more stays `APPROVED` and nothing is dispatched for it until F5.

Re-approval restarts at spec review. An `APPROVED` flow dispatches `SPEC_REVIEW`, unless its latest job is a `SPEC_REVIEW` queued at or after `approvedAt` (a dispatch whose bookkeeping did not commit), which the engine adopts. A re-ask resets the feature's `state` to `PENDING` and `currentStep` to null.

An active eligible latest job returns wait; a RUNNING flow without a job dispatches SPEC_REVIEW. A job ending FAILED, CANCELLED or CRASHED stops step_failed; a non-RUN job ending ESCALATED does too. Detail is `<STEP> job <id> <state>: <stateReason or 'no reason'>`. RUN ESCALATED remains eligible for its PR path, rather than this generic stop. No failed-step retry.

**Scope** — In: shared pure decision types, approval/start/wait/failure rules, the explicitly required ESCALATED RUN-with-PR handoff to REVIEW, and unit tests. Out: completed review/PLAN rules (US-008), remaining RUN/REVIEW/FIX progression and PR-wait/ready rules (US-009), service-side recovery recording (US-013). Flows with more than one feature, feature order, merge waits and independent features (fleet flow F5); F3 leaves such a flow `APPROVED`. Retrying a failed step: any failure stops the flow; a stopped flow is never restarted in place.

**Interface** — `FlowJobView`, `FlowStepInput`, `FlowStepAction`, `FlowStopReason`, `decideFlowStep`.
```ts
export type FlowStepAction =
  | { kind: 'skip' }                                   // not single-feature
  | { kind: 'wait' }
  | { kind: 'complete' }
  | { kind: 'stop'; reason: FlowStopReason; detail: string }
  | { kind: 'dispatch'; step: FlowStep; pr?: { number: number; headSha?: string } };
```
Stop reasons: `step_failed`, `verdict_unreadable`, `review_findings`, `plan_no_result`, `run_no_pr`, `pr_not_ready`, `cost_cap`, `creator_lost_access`, `budget_paused`, `dispatch_refused`.

userStories.title: Step decision, reviews and plan
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the pure decision engine through strict spec review, PLAN results and strict PRD review.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — `decideFlowStep` for `COMPLETED` `SPEC_REVIEW`, `PRD_REVIEW` and `PLAN` jobs: the verdict rule and the `PLAN` result rule.

Review steps stop strictly. F3 reads only the final verdict JSON of a review `AGENT` job. No findings: the flow continues. Any finding, or no parseable verdict: the flow stops with the findings in its detail. F4 replaces "any finding stops" with classify, fix and ask.

AGENT verdict rule (F2): an `AGENT` job ends `COMPLETED` only when `nax agents run` reported status `completed`; `failed`, `timeout` and `cancelled` end the job `FAILED`. So a `COMPLETED` review job's `agentResult.status` is always `completed`, and `agentResult.output` keeps the last 8,192 bytes, where the verdict sits.

For completed reviews, call parseFlowVerdict; no findings dispatches PLAN after SPEC_REVIEW or RUN after PRD_REVIEW. Findings stop review_findings with formatFindings detail. Missing/unparseable output stops verdict_unreadable with `<STEP> job <id>: no verdict JSON in the agent output`. Completed PLAN must contain both resultBranch and resultSha to dispatch PRD_REVIEW; either absent stops plan_no_result. Extend the shared decision tests rather than creating another decision engine.

**Scope** — In: completed review/PLAN decisions and preservation of active-review waiting. Out: parsing implementation (US-002), RUN/REVIEW/FIX outcomes (US-009), dispatch refs (US-010). Verdict classification (`answered`/`minor`/`ambiguous`), spec-fix jobs, batched questions, agent rulings on open PR items and the flow's ticket (fleet flow F4).

**Interface** — `decideFlowStep(input: FlowStepInput): FlowStepAction`; `parseFlowVerdict`, `formatFindings`.

userStories.title: Step decision, run, review and fix
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete the pure step engine with ingest-aware RUN PR waits and the one-REVIEW/one-FIX completion path.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — PR phase = `REVIEW` then one `FIX`. `REVIEW` goes through the existing head claim, so auto-review cannot double-dispatch. A `COMPLETED` `FIX` whose `fixReady.markedReady` is true completes the feature; any other `COMPLETED` `FIX` end stops the flow as `pr_not_ready`. Failed, cancelled, crashed or escalated FIX jobs retain the generic `step_failed` rule. Agent rulings for open items are F4.

`RUN` waits for its PR. `resultPrUrl` is filled by bundle ingest, after the job ends. A `COMPLETED` or `ESCALATED` `RUN` (a draft PR escalates at ingest) with no PR yet waits until its `FleetBundleIngest` row for the job's lease is `done`, `partial` or `failed`, or until `FLEET_FLOW_PR_WAIT_MS` (default 1,800,000) has passed since `finishedAt`; then it stops as `run_no_pr`.

A terminal eligible RUN with parsed PR dispatches REVIEW with number and RUN.resultSha as headSha. A completed REVIEW dispatches FIX using the feature's prNumber. A completed FIX with markedReady true completes; otherwise stop pr_not_ready with readyHeld or `FIX ended without a ready result`. Generic failure-state rules remain authoritative for failed/cancelled/crashed/escalated FIX and REVIEW. Extend existing decision tests.

**Scope** — In: pure RUN/REVIEW/FIX progression, timeout boundary and preservation of generic job-failure precedence. Out: reading PR URLs/repos/ingest rows (US-012), claim orchestration (US-016), dispatch bodies (US-010). Verdict classification (`answered`/`minor`/`ambiguous`), spec-fix jobs, batched questions, agent rulings on open PR items and the flow's ticket (fleet flow F4). Retrying a failed step: any failure stops the flow; a stopped flow is never restarted in place.

userStories.title: Step dispatch bodies and the remaining cap
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build each step's exact dispatch body and compute a safely rounded remaining per-flow cap.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — Refs. `SPEC_REVIEW` runs at `flow.specSha`. `PLAN` runs at `flow.branch` with `planFrom` = the spec path, and gets `expectBranch` like a thread `PLAN`, so a thread entry's local-only branch is used. `PRD_REVIEW` runs at the `PLAN` job's `resultSha` and reviews `.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json` (where `nax plan` writes it) against the spec. `RUN` runs at the `PLAN` job's `resultBranch`.

Every flow job is pinned to `flow.pinnedRunnerId` when it is set (thread entry); nax-entry flows have none.

Review agent = api setting. `FLEET_FLOW_REVIEW_AGENT` (default `Explore`) names the nax agent of both review steps; the model is always the flow's `reviewerRole`; the task starts with `/spec-review` so nax expands the skill.

Cap. `spentUsd` is recomputed on every tick as the sum of `costSpentUsd + costCarriedUsd` over jobs with the flow's id. Before any dispatch, a remaining cap (`costCapUsd - spentUsd`, rounded down to 4 decimals) below `0.0001` stops the flow (`cost_cap`); otherwise the remaining cap is the job's `maxCostUsd`. A job with unknown cost adds 0.

Use Decimal subtraction/rounding, returning null below the threshold. For an unpinned flow, both review-agent bodies have exactly repoId, command AGENT, feature, selected ref, bashMode raw, remaining numeric maxCostUsd and agent { name, task, model }, with no profiles or extra keys. For a pinned flow, add pinnedRunnerId to every step's body, including both AGENT review bodies. PLAN/RUN/REVIEW/FIX use profiles []. REVIEW/FIX bodies have prNumber but no ref/feature. Missing PLAN context for RUN throws an Error naming the missing plan. Omit pinnedRunnerId entirely when null. expectBranch is built by assign-payload, not an extra dispatch-body key.

**Scope** — In: pure cap and DTO-body builders. Out: config/env loading (US-017), job insert and expectBranch assignment (US-004), permission checks (US-014). Running `REVIEW` and `FIX` on the reviewer role's model: flow `PLAN`, `RUN`, `REVIEW` and `FIX` jobs use the default profile chain (`profiles: []`). Enforcing the cap inside `AGENT`, `PLAN`, `REVIEW` or `FIX` jobs beyond the `maxCostUsd` each job already receives.

**Interface** — `remainingCapUsd(capUsd, spentUsd): string | null` and `buildStepDispatch(input): DispatchFleetJobDto`.

userStories.title: The review head claim service
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose a bounded review-head claim API without exposing the reviews module's private repository.

**Motivation** — F3 builds that engine for one feature; verdict classification and spec fixes (F4), multi-feature order and merge waits (F5) and the web pages (F6) build on it.

**Approach** — `REVIEW` claim states (a new exported `FleetReviewClaimService` in the reviews module, since the review repository is module-private): no row → claimed; a row with a job → owned (adopted); a `pending` row younger than `prReviewPollMs` → busy (wait); an older `pending` row (a dead pass's claim, as `ReviewHeadDispatcher.reopenStaleClaim` treats it) → removed, then claimed; a `failed:*` row → stop `dispatch_refused`. Adoption (`FleetJobsService.adoptForFlow`) runs in the record transaction, after the flow-state check, with its audit entry. Any dispatch error after a claim releases the claim before the error is handled or rethrown.

This story returns the claim outcome; the flow caller owns adoption/stop behavior. Try insertPending, then findHead when insertion loses; a missing row after a lost insert is busy. A pending row is stale only when strictly older than prReviewPollMs, matching the existing dispatcher; remove and retry insertion without assuming the retry wins. All writes run under bookkeeping('fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping', ...). Add the provider/export to FleetReviewsModule and update its unit wiring expectations if pinned. Keep the repository module-private and preserve existing auto-review dispatcher behavior.

**Scope** — In: claimHead, markDispatched, release and service export/DB-free DI unit tests, preserving FleetReviewEventsService export. Out: flow-specific REVIEW dispatch/adoption/stop orchestration (US-016). Reading the PR head from the forge for the `REVIEW` claim: the claim uses the `RUN` job's `resultSha`.

**Interface** — `claimHead(repoId, prNumber, headSha, now): Promise<HeadClaim>`, `markDispatched(claimId, jobId)` and `release(claimId)`; outcomes `{ kind: 'claimed', claimId }`, `{ kind: 'owned', jobId }`, `{ kind: 'busy' }`, `{ kind: 'failed', outcome }`.

userStories.title: Advance, decide phase
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement the transaction-bounded decision phase, spend reconciliation and audited stop/completion writes.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — `advance(flowId, now)` runs three phases.

Decide (one transaction). Unlocked read of the flow and its latest job. When the next step can be `SPEC_REVIEW` or `PLAN` on a nax-entry flow, read the repo with `findReviewRepo` and the forge head of `flow.branch` before the transaction (a `RepoCheckException` ends this pass for the flow with nothing written); when the latest job is a `RUN` with a `resultPrUrl`, read the repo for `prNumberFor`. Then lock parent and flow; return when the parent is gone or the state is not `APPROVED` or `RUNNING`; update `spentUsd` if the sum changed; build `FlowStepInput` from the latest flow job and call `decideFlowStep`. `stop` and `complete` actions are written here. A `dispatch` action passes the guards in order: cap, creator access, then (for `SPEC_REVIEW` and `PLAN`) the spec sha; the first failing guard stops or re-asks instead.

This story implements decision/stop/complete/spend/PR lookup; dispatch guards and forge SHA checks are completed by US-014/015 before ticker wiring.

PR number. When the latest job is a `RUN` with a `resultPrUrl`, `advance` reads the repo with `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo(flow.repoId)` and parses the number with `prNumberFor({ provider: 'github', owner, name }, resultPrUrl)` (flows are GitHub-only: `AGENT`, `REVIEW` and `FIX` refuse GitLab). The `REVIEW` claim key is the `RUN` job's `resultSha`: the head the `RUN` pushed; nothing else writes the feature branch between the `RUN` and the flow's `REVIEW`. The `FIX` needs only the PR number.

Audit. Every flow write the engine makes is covered, inside the transaction that writes it: each stop, completion, step record and job adoption records an `AuditRecorder` entry with key `system.flow.advance`, resource type `flow`; `setSpent` runs under a new bookkeeping reason `fleet.flow-bookkeeping`; claim writes run under the existing `fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping`. `setSpent` is called only when the sum differs from the stored `spentUsd`.

Stop details are at most 2,000 characters (`FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX`).

Lock order is parent, then flow. Use thread lockForFlowTransition for thread entry and repos.lockById for nax entry. Re-read authoritative state/job context under locks. Activities are SYSTEM/flow; flow.stopped carries { flowId, stopReason, detail, step, jobId }; flow.completed accompanies complete. Add fleet.flow-bookkeeping to BOOKKEEPING_REASONS and EXPECTED_REASON_IDS in audit-coverage.bookkeeping.spec.ts, not a blanket exemption for state writes.

**Scope** — In: advance service skeleton, decide phase, stop/complete/activity/audit and spend bookkeeping. Out: actual dispatch/record (US-013), cap/access guards (US-014), spec checks/reask (US-015), REVIEW claims (US-016). Recomputing `spentUsd` after a flow has stopped or completed, when a late ingest raises a job's cost. Notifications on a flow stop or completion: until F4, a stop is visible only in flow activity, audit, `stopReason` and `stopDetail`.

**Interface** — `FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance(flowId: string, now: Date): Promise<void>`.

userStories.title: Advance, dispatch and record phases
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Dispatch non-REVIEW steps outside transactions and record progress without overwriting a concurrent stop/re-ask.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — Dispatch (no transaction held). `REVIEW` goes through `FleetReviewClaimService`; every other step calls `jobs.dispatch(flow.createdById, flow.projectId, buildStepDispatch(...), { flowId, flowStep, auditKey: 'system.flow.advance' })`.

Record (one transaction). Lock parent and flow; if the flow is still `APPROVED` or `RUNNING`, adopt the job when the claim was owned, mark the step (`APPROVED` becomes `RUNNING` with activity `flow.started`), record activity `flow.step` and the audit entry.

REVIEW-specific orchestration/adoption is US-016; here implement every other step with the exact body selected by decideFlowStep/buildStepDispatch.

Dispatch refusals stop. `BudgetPausedException` stops as `budget_paused`; `ConflictAppException`, `ValidationAppException`, `NotFoundAppException` and `FleetDispatchException` stop as `dispatch_refused` with detail `<STEP>: <reason>`, where the reason is the `ValidationAppException`'s `args.reason` when it is a string and the exception's class name otherwise (the `ReviewHeadDispatcher` rule). Any other error propagates, the ticker logs it, and the next tick tries again.

A human stop does not cancel the running job (design, Stops). The record phase writes nothing when the flow has meanwhile left `APPROVED`/`RUNNING`. `IFleetFlowRepository.stop` now also marks every feature `STOPPED`, for every caller.

The job row is the source of truth. Every flow job stores `flowId` and `flowStep` in the same insert that creates it. The engine reads the flow's latest job (by `queuedAt`) on every tick, so a crash between dispatch and the bookkeeping that follows loses nothing: the next tick sees the job. `FleetFlowFeature.state`, `currentStep` and `prNumber` are written after each dispatch; the `FIX` step reads `prNumber` from the feature.

For APPROVED recovery, recognize a SPEC_REVIEW queued at/after approvedAt rather than dispatching it twice; reconcile missing progress with audit/activity in a record transaction. Record flow.started only on APPROVED -> RUNNING and include approvalMode/approverId. flow.step payload is { step, jobId }. Stop/complete/record/adoption audits use system.flow.advance, resourceType flow in the writing transaction. Activities use actorType SYSTEM/actorId flow. Retain guard seams for US-014/015.

**Scope** — In: non-REVIEW dispatch/record, exact option seam, failure mapping and durable recovery. Out: cap/creator guards (US-014), SHA reask (US-015), REVIEW claims (US-016). Cancelling a running job when a flow stops or returns to `PENDING`: by design the flow only starts nothing more. Retrying a failed step: any failure stops the flow; a stopped flow is never restarted in place. The next tick retry after an unexpected dispatch error is recovery of a pass, not a retry of a failed job step.

**Interface** — `FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance(flowId: string, now: Date): Promise<void>`; `jobs.dispatch(flow.createdById, flow.projectId, buildStepDispatch(...), { flowId, flowStep, auditKey: 'system.flow.advance' })`.

[unit] After that dispatch, advance records activity flow.started with approvalMode and approverId in its payload, actorType SYSTEM and actorId flow.
[unit] After that dispatch, advance records activity flow.step with payload { step: 'SPEC_REVIEW', jobId: 'j1' }.

userStories.title: Dispatch guards: cap and creator access
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop new step dispatches when the cap is exhausted or the original creator can no longer dispatch in the project.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, Steps, Cost cap, Stops) asks for a deterministic engine that chains the existing jobs, checks the cap between jobs and stops instead of retrying.

**Approach** — Creator access. Before each dispatch the creator must still exist, not be disabled, and hold `fleet.job.dispatch` in the flow's project (`mayDispatch` from `apps/api/src/fleet/schedules/schedule-access.ts` over the step repository's `creatorAccess` and `PermissionService.effectiveKeys`); otherwise the flow stops as `creator_lost_access`.

Cap. `spentUsd` is recomputed on every tick as the sum of `costSpentUsd + costCarriedUsd` over jobs with the flow's id. Before any dispatch, a remaining cap (`costCapUsd - spentUsd`, rounded down to 4 decimals) below `0.0001` stops the flow (`cost_cap`); otherwise the remaining cap is the job's `maxCostUsd`. A job with unknown cost adds 0.

A `dispatch` action passes the guards in order: cap, creator access, then (for `SPEC_REVIEW` and `PLAN`) the spec sha; the first failing guard stops or re-asks instead.

Use the freshly reconciled spend, remainingCapUsd and buildStepDispatch, not floating-point subtraction. cost_cap detail is `spent <spent> of cap <cap>`. Resolve PrincipalRef from createdByType/createdById, check effectiveKeys in { projectId: flow.projectId }, and reuse mayDispatch for both user and agent. Stops use the existing audited stop path and bounded detail. The approver/system principal's permissions must not substitute for the creator's.

**Scope** — In: cap-first and creator-access guards before each dispatch, remaining cap propagation. Out: pure arithmetic (US-010), creator row lookup (US-006), spec guard (US-015). Enforcing the cap inside `AGENT`, `PLAN`, `REVIEW` or `FIX` jobs beyond the `maxCostUsd` each job already receives. userStories.title: Spec change before PLAN
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reuse F1 approval invalidation whenever the spec SHA changes before SPEC_REVIEW or PLAN.

**Motivation** — F3 builds that engine for one feature; verdict classification and spec fixes (F4), multi-feature order and merge waits (F5) and the web pages (F6) build on it.

**Approach** — Spec check only before the flow's first push. Before dispatching `SPEC_REVIEW` or `PLAN` the engine compares the flow's `specSha` with the thread's `publishedSha` (thread entry) or the forge head of `flow.branch` (nax entry). Any difference re-asks through the F1 path (`PENDING`, new `fleet.flow.start` request, new `specSha`). After `PLAN` pushes, the branch moves by the flow's own commits and the PRD freezes the spec, so no later step checks. The forge head is read only when the next step can be `SPEC_REVIEW` or `PLAN`: the flow is `APPROVED`, has no flow job yet, or its latest job is a terminal `SPEC_REVIEW`.

`FleetFlowsService.respec`: its re-ask branch moves into a new public `reaskLocked(flow: FleetFlowRecord, specSha: string, now: Date): Promise<FleetFlowRecord>` (close the old request if any with reason `superseded`, open a new `fleet.flow.start` request, `flows.reask`, audit `system.flow.respec`, activity `flow.respec`), which `respec` calls; the caller holds the locks.

Before a nax-entry candidate's transaction, findReviewRepo and mintReadOnlyToken/getBranchHead; never hold a transaction across forge HTTP and never log/store the token. A RepoCheckException resolves the pass with no writes and no dispatch. If the parent can still be locked and the flow remains advanceable, a missing review-repo lookup or githubInstallationId null stops dispatch_refused with `<STEP>: repo not connected`. A parent gone at lock time instead returns without writes, as required by the parent-lock gate. For a thread entry use publishedSha from the locked parent, including local-only branches. In the decide transaction apply cap then creator access then this SHA guard. Preserve respec's updateSha carry-forward behavior and avoid duplicate audit/activity after extraction. Reask resets feature state/currentStep through US-003 and does not cancel any running job.

**Scope** — In: reaskLocked extraction, thread/forge SHA checks, transient forge failure semantics and preserving respec's existing carry-forward branch. Out: dispatch/cap/access implementations (US-013/014), spec-fix jobs (F4). Re-checking the spec sha after `PLAN` has been dispatched, and reacting to a thread re-publish while a flow is `RUNNING` (the F1 listener ignores it). Cancelling a running job when a flow stops or returns to `PENDING`: by design the flow only starts nothing more.

userStories.title: REVIEW through the head claim
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Dispatch or adopt the RUN head's REVIEW without duplicating auto-review, releasing claims on dispatch failures.

**Motivation** — F3 builds that engine for one feature; verdict classification and spec fixes (F4), multi-feature order and merge waits (F5) and the web pages (F6) build on it.

**Approach** — `REVIEW` claim states (a new exported `FleetReviewClaimService` in the reviews module, since the review repository is module-private): no row → claimed; a row with a job → owned (adopted); a `pending` row younger than `prReviewPollMs` → busy (wait); an older `pending` row (a dead pass's claim, as `ReviewHeadDispatcher.reopenStaleClaim` treats it) → removed, then claimed; a `failed:*` row → stop `dispatch_refused`. Adoption (`FleetJobsService.adoptForFlow`) runs in the record transaction, after the flow-state check, with its audit entry. Any dispatch error after a claim releases the claim before the error is handled or rethrown.

The `REVIEW` claim key is the `RUN` job's `resultSha`: the head the `RUN` pushed; nothing else writes the feature branch between the `RUN` and the flow's `REVIEW`. The `FIX` needs only the PR number.

Call claimHead(repoId, pr.number, pr.headSha, now) outside the dispatch transaction. claimed dispatches the exact REVIEW body with flowId/flowStep/auditKey, then markDispatched links the claim to the returned job. owned never dispatches: lock parent/flow in the record phase, check APPROVED/RUNNING, call jobs.adoptForFlow, markStep REVIEW/prNumber and record flow.step and system.flow.advance audit in that transaction. Adoption false stops dispatch_refused with `REVIEW: head claimed by another flow`. busy returns with no step/stop; failed stops dispatch_refused with `REVIEW: <outcome>`. Any newly claimed dispatch error releases the claim first; BudgetPausedException stops budget_paused, declared refusal exceptions stop dispatch_refused, plain errors rethrow. If the flow has stopped/re-asked before record, do not adopt or write progress.

**Scope** — In: REVIEW claim/dispatch/adoption/record and release semantics. Out: claim-service internals (US-011), permission/cap guards (US-014), alternative FIX/ruling loops (F4). Reading the PR head from the forge for the `REVIEW` claim: the claim uses the `RUN` job's `resultSha`. Running `REVIEW` and `FIX` on the reviewer role's model: flow `PLAN`, `RUN`, `REVIEW` and `FIX` jobs use the default profile chain (`profiles: []`).

**Interface** — `FleetReviewClaimService.claimHead(repoId, prNumber, headSha, now): Promise<HeadClaim>`; `markDispatched(claimId, jobId)`; `release(claimId)`; `FleetJobsService.adoptForFlow(jobId: string, flowId: string, step: FlowStep): Promise<boolean>`.

userStories.title: The flow ticker and its config
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire the finished single-feature engine into a bounded, creator-attributed, single-flight API ticker.

**Motivation** — F1 (`fleet-flow-record`, #400) records flows and their one approval, and F2 (`fleet-agent-job`, #403) added the `AGENT` job kind, but nothing moves an approved flow: `FleetFlowStartCommand.execute` and the thread tick both leave it `APPROVED` and stop.

**Approach** — `FleetFlowTicker.poll()` returns at once while a pass runs; otherwise it calls `tick(new Date())`. `tick(now)` pages through advanceable flows and, for each, runs `advance(id, now)` inside `runAsSystem('flow', ..., { onBehalfOf: { type: createdByType, id: createdById } })`, logging and continuing on error.

Ticker only, no event hook. Nothing fires on approval or on a job's end; the ticker finds the work within one interval. Steps take minutes to hours, so up to 30 s of delay is acceptable, and a tick is crash-safe where an in-process event is not.

Actor. Each flow is advanced inside `runAsSystem('flow', ..., { onBehalfOf: { type: createdByType, id: createdById } })`, as `FixFollowUpSubscriber` does, so `actorTypeFor` records an agent creator as `AGENT`. Flow jobs are dispatched through `FleetJobsService.dispatch` with `createdById` as requester and the new system key `system.flow.advance` as `auditKey`. The ticker declares `@SystemWriter('system.flow.advance')`.

Paging. `listAdvanceable(limit, afterId)` returns single-feature `APPROVED`/`RUNNING` flows ordered by `id`, after the given id; the ticker pages 50 at a time until a short page, at most 10 pages per tick. A new index `FleetFlow(state, id)` serves it.

Config bounds. `FLEET_FLOW_TICK_MS` 1,000-3,600,000; `FLEET_FLOW_PR_WAIT_MS` 60,000-86,400,000; `FLEET_FLOW_REVIEW_AGENT` must match `AGENT_NAME_RE`; all three are validated by the Joi schema in `apps/api/src/config/env.validation.ts`.

Add flowTickMs (default 30,000), flowPrWaitMs (default 1,800,000) and flowReviewAgent (default Explore) to IFleetConfig, FleetConfigSchema, factory and testFleetConfig; update pinned config tests. onModuleInit starts no interval when sweepEnabled is false; otherwise start an unref'ed configurable interval, clear it on destroy, and reset poll's single-flight flag in finally. Errors log the failing flow id without stopping subsequent flows.

Neither imported module reaches FlowsModule, so there is no import cycle. Remove system.flow.advance from PENDING_SURFACE_KEYS and permission-contract.spec.ts expectedPending; system-writer.decorator.spec.ts gains [FleetFlowTicker, 'system.flow.advance'], length 40 -> 41 and asserts pending false.
